headline: Approved new alcohol rules for bars and restaurants, including an 18-to-20 event permit and a January 29, 2027 application deadline.
summary: Restaurants must serve suitable food at all hours of alcohol service. Licensed managers must be on premises for at least 50% of alcohol service hours. Complaints about two pawn shops and a club were referred to police.
decisions: Approved special one-day wine and beer licenses for Hive Public Market events.
Approved special one-day wine and beer licenses for Lowell Community Charter Public School events.
Approved a special 18-to-20 event permit for Tuscabar Performance Center.
Approved a victualler license for Corner Crust & Crumb.
Approved a Class 2 dealer license for Angels Auto Care.
Approved Section 1 of the alcohol regulations, covering bar and restaurant rules, 4-0.
Approved Section 2, creating the special 18-to-20 event permit, 4-0.
Approved Section 3, on manager responsibilities and promoter rules, 4-0.
Set 12:00 noon on January 29, 2027, as the deadline to submit license change applications.
Continued the hearing on Showcase Cinema Lowell's license transfer to November 19, 2026.
Referred the complaint about Lowell Pawn, 755 Lakeview Avenue, to the Lowell Police Department for investigation.
Referred the complaint about Prasat Meas Jewelry & Pawn, 28 Branch Street, to the police department.
Referred the complaint about Club Passe-Temps of Lowell, 369-371 Moody Street, to the Lowell Police Department.
discussion: Restaurant food sales test: Members asked how the 35% food-sales cutoff would be checked and how a substantial menu change would be judged. The attorney said some legal terms, such as substantial, involve judgment.
Under-21 event hours: Members asked whether the 18-to-20 permit should have a time limit. The proposal has no hours limit, and the rules could be amended later.
License change timing: Members discussed a filing deadline for restaurants and bars switching license types, since state approval can take months.
Private clubs: Members asked whether the rules affect private clubs. The answer given was that members-only clubs are not affected.
Complaint jurisdiction: Some complaints about private clubs may fall outside the commission's authority. The law department is reviewing them and will report at the next meeting.
